body: ISO/IEC 42005:2025 provides a standardised framework for conducting AI system impact assessments -- the structured process of identifying, analysing, and evaluating the potential effects of an AI system on individuals, groups, and society before deployment. It is the companion standard to ISO/IEC 42001 (AI management system requirements) and fills the gap between the management-system governance layer and the per-system technical risk assessment required by EU AI Act Article 9 and Colorado SB 205. For a verification-first operator, ISO 42005 is the assay protocol: it defines what you measure, how you weight the findings, which stakeholders you consult, and how you document the residual risk before you sign a verified measurement credential. The Council of AI treats 42005 as the measurement rubric, not a paperwork exercise. Concretely: (1) the impact assessment produces a structured JSON artifact (not a PDF report) that can be independently signed. (2) The artifact feeds the Council of AI Containment Incident Index as a pre-deployment baseline, so post-market deviations are detectable. (3) Cross-jurisdiction mapping (EU AI Act Annex IV, ISO 42005, NIST AI RMF) is maintained as a live reference table. The posture is monitored containment, not provable isolation -- an impact assessment proves you looked before you leapt, not that nothing can go wrong.
context: 2026-09-01 engine cycle -- ISO/IEC 42005:2025 published; the companion impact-assessment standard to ISO/IEC 42001 (AI management systems) is now the reference for structured AI impact assessment in conformity workflows.
